title: Google Ads for Construction Companies: 2026 PPC Guide

facts.fact: The page states that average project contract values range from $50,000 for luxury residential remodels to $5,000,000+ for commercial general contracting.
facts.quote: With average project contract values ranging from **$50,000 for luxury residential remodels** to **$5,000,000+ for commercial general contracting**

facts.fact: The page's table lists the average CPC for commercial general contractors in Tier 1 metros as $45.00 - $140.00.
The page's table lists the average CPC for luxury custom home builders in Tier 1 metros as $35.00 - $95.00.
The page's table lists the average CPC for commercial roofing contractors in Tier 1 metros as $55.00 - $160.00.
The page's table lists the average CPC for high-end kitchen and home remodeling in Tier 1 metros as $25.00 - $65.00.
The page's table lists the average CPC for civil and industrial concrete contractors in Tier 1 metros as $35.00 - $110.00.
The page states that a single click can cost $100 in construction Google Ads.
facts.quote: Because a single click can cost $100, **you cannot afford a single wasted click**.

facts.fact: The page states that over 65% of wasted ad spend in construction campaigns originates from three toxic query categories.

facts.fact: The page states that over 70% of qualified construction leads arrive via telephone calls rather than online form fills.
facts.quote: In construction and contracting, **over 70% of qualified leads arrive via telephone calls**, not online form fills.

facts.fact: The page recommends setting a minimum call duration of 90 seconds before CallRail fires a Qualified Call conversion into Google Ads.
facts.quote: Set a minimum call duration threshold (e.g., **90 seconds**) before CallRail fires a conversion event (`Qualified Call`) back into Google Ads.

facts.fact: The page cites residential consumers looking for $150 handyman fixes as an example of low-ticket searches that waste construction ad spend.
facts.quote: residential consumers looking for $150 handyman fixes.

facts.fact: The page recommends displaying a $5M+ General Liability insurance badge next to the primary CTA on a construction company's site.
facts.quote: State Contractor License number, $5M+ General Liability insurance badge, and OSHA safety compliance badges displayed immediately next to the primary CTA.

facts.fact: The page gives an example of a minimum project threshold a construction firm could state on its site, setting it at projects exceeding $75,000.
Google Local Service Ads operate on a Pay-Per-Lead model rather than Pay-Per-Click, so the advertiser pays only when an authorized caller contacts the business directly.
facts.quote: Operates on a **Pay-Per-Lead (PPL)** model rather than Pay-Per-Click: you only pay when an authorized caller contacts your business directly.

facts.fact: Google Local Service Ads appear at the top of Google search results, above traditional text ads, and are marked with the Google Guaranteed green badge.
facts.quote: LSAs appear at the absolute top of Google search results, above traditional text ads.

facts.fact: The page recommends that qualifying residential construction contractors and remodelers activate Google Local Service Ads in addition to standard Google Search Ads.
facts.quote: qualifying residential construction contractors and remodelers should activate **Google Local Service Ads (LSAs)**

facts.fact: The guide is titled as a 2026 PPC guide for Google Ads for construction companies.
